title: Guide: the guess alone
description: The abstraction proposes every set of at most k nodes and the check accepts them all, so the number of solutions is the number of candidates. See the guide page "Why a loop".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% The graph of the guide's figures: ten nodes, fifteen edges.
node(1..10).
edge(1,2). edge(1,3). edge(1,4). edge(2,3). edge(2,4). edge(3,4).
edge(4,5). edge(4,6). edge(5,6). edge(6,7). edge(6,8). edge(7,8).
edge(8,9). edge(8,10). edge(9,10).
fragments.description: The graph. Added to every solver.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most k nodes to delete.
{ del(V) : node(V) } k.
#show del/1.
fragments.description: Proposes candidates (solver A): at most k deleted nodes.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The check sees which nodes are deleted.
glue(del(V)) :- node(V).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the deleted nodes.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% No counterexample ever: every candidate is accepted.
#false.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)
